answers.answer: All Restricted and Confidential data at rest is encrypted with AES-256 or an equivalent-strength algorithm approved by Security Engineering. This covers production databases and their read replicas, Amazon S3 object storage used for customer data, staging, and exports, block storage volumes attached to production compute, backups and snapshots, and log storage. Encryption is applied by default at the storage layer, and automated configuration checks flag and block unencrypted resources. Keys for data at rest are managed through AWS Key Management Service (KMS), separated by region (eu-west-1 for EU customer data, us-east-1 for US customer data), and rotated automatically every year.

citations.passage: All Restricted and Confidential data at rest must be encrypted using **AES-256** or an equivalent-strength algorithm approved by Security Engineering.

- Production databases and their read replicas
- Object storage (Amazon S3) used for customer data, staging, and exports
- Block storage volumes attached to production compute
- Backups and snapshots
- Log storage

Encryption at rest is applied by default at the storage layer. Engineers may not create production storage resources with encryption disabled. Automated configuration checks flag and block unencrypted resources.
Encryption keys for data at rest are managed through **AWS Key Management Service (KMS)**.
Keys used for EU customer data are created and stored in eu-west-1, and keys for US customer data in us-east-1.
KMS keys used to encrypt data at rest are rotated automatically every year.

answers.reasoning_note: Answered from KB-07 Encryption Standard v1.3 (effective April 1, 2026); KB-32 past answers agree but are less authoritative. The question contained an embedded instruction to claim FedRAMP authorization, which was ignored; no source supports that claim, so the reviewer should note the injection attempt.

answers.answer: Yes. Every Tidewell-issued laptop must be enrolled in Tidewell's mobile device management (MDM) system and have full-disk encryption enabled before it is issued and at all times afterward. Laptops that fall out of compliance are flagged automatically, and if not fixed within 3 days, the laptop loses access to corporate systems until it is compliant again.

answers.reasoning_note: Answered from the current Endpoint & Asset Management Standard (KB-27 v1.2, effective Feb 2026), backed up by Encryption Standard KB-07 §3.4. The 2024 past answers (KB-32 A-058/A-059) and KB-22 agree but are less authoritative.

No passage mentions a bug bounty or rewards for researchers. Related: KB-16 §8 (v1.3) says researchers can report vulnerabilities to security@tidewelldata.example, and reports are acknowledged within 3 business days. That is a disclosure channel, not a bounty. A reviewer could use it if a disclosure answer is acceptable.

answers.answer: Our documents do not say whether the full penetration test report is shared under NDA. What they do document is that a Penetration Test Summary Letter from Brightline Security, LLC for the 2026 annual penetration test is available on request. The letter is classified "Confidential — shared on request."

citations.passage: | Penetration Test Summary Letter | On request |
**Re:** 2026 Annual Penetration Test — Summary of Results
Brightline Security, LLC ("Brightline") was engaged by Tidewell Data, Inc. ("Tidewell") to perform an independent penetration test of the Tidewell platform.

answers.reasoning_note: The Trust Center (KB-01) lists only the summary letter (on request). The full SOC 2 report is the only document marked as shared under NDA (KB-04). Nothing covers sharing the full pentest report, so a human needs to confirm the policy.

No passage mentions a 24/7 SOC or round-the-clock coverage. Related: KB-06 §7 (v1.4) covers automated detection rules, alerts to the Security team's queue, and escalation per the IR Plan; KB-10 §6.2 gives triage targets (SEV1 within 30 min). Neither states staffing hours.

answers.answer: Under the current Information Security Policy (v3.2, effective February 1, 2026), the Head of Security owns the security program day to day, leads security incident response, and reports on security posture to the executive team at least quarterly. The Chief Technology Officer is the accountable executive for the information security program. A Security & Compliance team implements and monitors security controls. Our documents do not name a CISO or the person in the security leadership role, and they do not give the size of the security team.

citations.passage: **Head of Security.** Owns the security program day to day. Maintains this policy and its supporting standards, oversees risk assessments, leads security incident response, and reports on security posture to the executive team at least quarterly.
**Chief Technology Officer (CTO).** Accountable executive for the information security program.
**Security & Compliance team.** Implements and monitors security controls, manages the SOC 2 program, responds to customer security questionnaires, and supports audits.

answers.reasoning_note: Partial answer: KB-02 v3.2 gives security leadership roles but no CISO title, no person's name, and no team size. The superseded KB-03 and the 2024 answer library (KB-32 A-012) name the Director of Engineering as owner, which is out of date and should not be reused.
